items.name: Monterey Bay Aquarium
items.cost: $65 adults (18–69); $50 youth (5–17); $50 seniors (70+); free ages 4 and under
items.best_time: Check the daily schedule page for feeding and program times and plan around them; buy tickets in advance.
items.description: Large public aquarium at the end of Cannery Row with exhibits on Monterey Bay habitats and the open ocean, plus scheduled animal feedings and auditorium programs.
items.notes: The aquarium says hours vary by day and asks visitors to check its calendar; buy tickets ahead.

items.name: Cannery Row
items.best_time: Daytime walk combined with the Aquarium and San Carlos Beach; the official calendar lists seasonal events.
items.description: Waterfront street of former sardine canneries now filled with shops, restaurants and hotels, running from the Coast Guard pier area to the Aquarium.
items.notes: A public street: shops and restaurants set their own hours.

items.name: Old Fisherman's Wharf
items.best_time: Go in daylight to watch sea lions and harbor activity; it's also the departure point for whale-watching and bay cruises.
items.description: Historic wooden wharf in Monterey Harbor lined with seafood restaurants and shops, and home base for whale-watching, fishing, sailing and glass-bottom boat operators.
items.notes: Shops and restaurants on the wharf set their own hours.

site_link.label: Christmas on the Wharf on the holiday lights map

items.name: Monterey State Historic Park (Custom House Plaza)
items.hours: Custom House, Pacific House and First Brick House: Tue–Sun 10am–4pm; gardens open daily
items.best_time: Tuesday–Sunday when the museum buildings are open; Thursday–Sunday if you want a guided walk.
items.description: State park preserving adobes and other buildings from Monterey's Mexican and early-statehood periods, centered on Custom House Plaza near Fisherman's Wharf.
items.notes: Park page lists no admission fee amounts. Gardens 'availability subject to events and weather.' No current restrictions listed (checked 11/25/2026).

items.name: Stevenson House
items.hours: Tours Fri & Sat at 10:00am and 3:30pm
items.best_time: Friday or Saturday; arrive early — tours are capped at 10 guests, first come first served.
items.description: Adobe in Monterey State Historic Park associated with author Robert Louis Stevenson's 1879 stay, shown on small guided tours.
items.notes: Larkin House tours run Fridays and Saturdays at 11:30am and 2pm. Admission isn't published.

items.name: Guided Walks & Path of History
items.hours: Guided walks Thu–Sun at 11am, 1pm and 3pm (about one hour, from the Custom House)
items.best_time: Thursday–Sunday for ranger/docent walks; any day for the self-guided route.
items.description: Hour-long guided walks through Old Monterey's historic buildings depart from the Custom House, and a two-mile self-guided Path of History can be done anytime with a brochure or phone.
items.notes: Self-guided brochures at Custom House or Pacific House. Guided-walk price not stated.

items.name: Colton Hall Museum
items.hours: Daily 10am–4pm
items.best_time: Any day 10–4; pair with the State Historic Park adobes a few blocks away.
items.description: City-run museum in the building where California's first constitutional convention met in 1849, with the Old Monterey Jail alongside.
items.notes: City pages disagree on days (daily vs Thursday–Sunday); call (831) 646-5640 before a weekday visit.

items.name: Presidio of Monterey Museum
items.address: 76th Artillery Street & Corporal Ewing Road, Bldg 113, Monterey, CA 93944
items.hours: Sat & Sun 10am–4pm
items.best_time: Weekends only; combine with the bay views in Lower Presidio Historic Park.
items.description: Small city museum in Lower Presidio Historic Park covering the site's military history from early Native and Spanish eras onward.
items.notes: The museum's own page says weekends; an older city page says Thursday–Sunday.

items.name: Royal Presidio Chapel (San Carlos Cathedral)
items.address: Royal Presidio Chapel (San Carlos Cathedral), Monterey, CA
items.best_time: Avoid Mass times; check the cathedral's site for current visiting hours.
items.description: Active Catholic church that dates to Monterey's Spanish colonial presidio, now the city's cathedral.
items.notes: Visiting hours aren't published; it is an active parish church.

items.name: Cooper-Molera Adobe
items.hours: Grounds daily 7am–4pm; museum Thu–Sun 10am–2pm
items.best_time: Thursday–Sunday morning for the museum; the gardens and café are open daily.
items.description: 1827 adobe complex in downtown Monterey run by the National Trust for Historic Preservation, with a small museum, historic gardens, a bakery-café and a restaurant.
items.notes: Across the street from Simoneau Plaza. Tour prices aren't published.

items.name: Whale watching from Old Fisherman's Wharf
items.best_time: Book directly with an operator and ask what's currently being sighted.
items.description: Several licensed charter operators run whale-watching trips out of Monterey Harbor from Old Fisherman's Wharf; the City harbor page lists them.
items.notes: The City lists Discovery Whale Watch, Monterey Bay Whale Watch and Princess Monterey Bay Whale Watching on the wharf; each sets its own prices and departures.

items.name: Monterey Bay Coastal Recreation Trail
items.address: Monterey Bay Coastal Recreation Trail, Monterey, CA
items.hours: City parks and beaches open daily; no one may remain 10 p.m.–6 a.m.
items.best_time: Morning walk or bike ride along the Cannery Row–Wharf–Del Monte stretch; keep right and ring before passing.
items.description: Paved multi-use path along the bayfront running 18 miles from Castroville to Pacific Grove, linking Monterey's wharves, beaches and Cannery Row.
items.notes: E-bikes allowed; no skateboards or motorized scooters; dogs on a 6-foot leash.

items.name: San Carlos Beach Park
items.address: Cannery Row at Reeside Avenue, Monterey, CA 93940
items.hours: City parks and beaches open daily; no one may remain 10 p.m.–6 a.m.
items.best_time: Calm mornings for divers and swimmers; check for wildlife closures before you go.
items.description: Small grassy beach park at the start of Cannery Row beside the boat launch ramp, popular with recreational scuba divers.
items.notes: Parking is paid. The City has closed access before when sea lions haul out.

items.name: Del Monte Beach
items.address: Tide Avenue and Surf Way, Monterey, CA 93940
items.hours: City parks and beaches open daily; no one may remain 10 p.m.–6 a.m.
items.best_time: Low-key beach walks east of Wharf II; no lifeguards, so stay out of rough surf.
items.description: Long sandy beach east of Municipal Wharf II that continues into Monterey State Beach.
items.notes: No lifeguards.

items.name: Monterey State Beach
items.address: Del Monte Avenue at Park Avenue, Monterey, CA 93940
items.hours: 8 AM – Sunset
items.best_time: Day use 8 a.m. to sunset; low tide for tidepools; never turn your back on the ocean.
items.description: State beach made up of three sandy beach areas about a mile apart, shared by Monterey and Seaside, used for surfing, beach walks and tidepooling.
items.notes: State Parks closes the sand during big swells and king tides; check its page first.

items.name: McAbee Beach
items.hours: City parks and beaches open daily; no one may remain 10 p.m.–6 a.m.
items.best_time: Brief stop while walking Cannery Row.
items.description: One of several small pocket beaches tucked between buildings along Cannery Row.

items.name: Kayaking & SUP – Monterey Bay Kayaks
items.address: Kayaking & SUP – Monterey Bay Kayaks, Monterey, CA
items.cost: $40 per person (single/double sit-on-top kayak or SUP, up to 4 hours)
items.hours: Nov & Dec: open 9–5 daily (Thanksgiving 9–3; Christmas Day closed)
items.best_time: Calm mornings; check the shop's beach cam/conditions first.
items.description: Paddle-sport outfitter with a Monterey shoreline location (plus one at Elkhorn Slough) renting kayaks and stand-up paddleboards and running tours on the bay.
items.notes: Closed Christmas Day; shorter hours on some holidays.

items.name: Jacks Peak County Park
items.address: Jacks Peak County Park, Monterey, CA
items.best_time: Clear mornings for bay and Carmel views from the forested ridge.
items.description: Monterey County day-use park on a pine-forested ridge above Monterey with hiking trails and picnic areas.
items.notes: The county's site blocks our checker, so hours and the day-use fee are unconfirmed.

items.name: Veterans Memorial Park
items.hours: City parks and beaches open daily; no one may remain 10 p.m.–6 a.m.
items.best_time: Daytime hike under the pines; gateway to Huckleberry Hill trails.
items.description: City park in the hills above downtown with pine-forest hiking trails, bay views and a first-come, first-served campground.
items.notes: Campsites cost extra. No fires in fire season (1 June–1 November).
items.geo_note: pinned at the neighbouring Huckleberry Hill preserve (same city address)

items.name: Huckleberry Hill Nature Preserve
items.hours: City parks and beaches open daily; no one may remain 10 p.m.–6 a.m.
items.best_time: Daytime; enter on foot via Veterans Memorial Park and carry the city trail map.
items.description: 81-acre city nature preserve of Monterey pine forest with a network of established hiking trails, reached on foot through Veterans Memorial Park.
items.notes: Fee not stated.

items.name: Lower Presidio Historic Park
items.hours: City parks and beaches open daily; no one may remain 10 p.m.–6 a.m.
items.best_time: Weekends to include the free Presidio museum; clear days for harbor views.
items.description: Hillside historic park above Lighthouse Curve with views over Monterey Harbor and the bay, home to the Presidio of Monterey Museum.

items.name: Point Lobos State Natural Reserve
items.hours: 8:00 a.m.–5 p.m. (no entry after 4:30 pm)
items.best_time: Arrive early — no entry after 4:30 pm and vehicles over 21 ft are not allowed.
items.description: State natural reserve three miles south of Carmel on Highway 1 with coastal trails, coves, cypress groves and a Whalers Cabin museum.
items.notes: No entry after 4:30pm. During big swells State Parks closes the reserve to cars (still open on foot).

items.name: 17-Mile Drive
items.best_time: Daylight hours for the coastal viewpoints.
items.description: Private scenic toll road through Pebble Beach and the Del Monte Forest with coastal turnouts between Pacific Grove and Carmel.
items.notes: Pebble Beach's site blocks our checker, so the toll and gate hours are unconfirmed.

items.name: Carmel Beach
items.best_time: Late afternoon; check city beach-fire rules before bringing a fire.
items.description: White-sand city beach at the foot of Carmel-by-the-Sea's village.
items.notes: Carmel's city site blocks our checker, so beach rules (including fires) are unconfirmed.

items.name: Carmel Mission Basilica
items.cost: Adults $15; Seniors (62+) $12; Youth (7-17) $8; Child (6 and under) Free
items.hours: Wed–Thu 10am–4pm; Fri–Sat 10am–5pm; Sun 11:30am–5pm; closed Mon–Tue
items.best_time: Wednesday–Sunday; closed Thanksgiving, Christmas Day and the day after.
items.description: Historic Spanish mission and active parish in Carmel; admission covers a self-guided visit of the basilica, museums and grounds.
items.notes: Closed Thanksgiving Day; the basilica can close for weddings and services.

items.name: Lovers Point Park & Beach
items.address: Ocean View Blvd. and 17th St., Pacific Grove, CA 93950
items.best_time: Calm days for swimming/snorkeling in the cove; walk the coastal path toward Point Pinos.
items.description: Waterfront city park on Pacific Grove's shoreline with lawns, sandy coves, rocky outcrops, a concrete pier, a children's pool and a restaurant.
items.notes: Stillwell Children's Pool is closed until summer 2027.

items.name: Point Pinos Lighthouse
items.hours: Thu 1pm–3pm; Fri, Sat & Sun 11am–3pm
items.best_time: Thursday–Sunday afternoons; closed Thanksgiving, Black Friday, Dec 25 and Jan 1.
items.description: Lighthouse at the tip of the Monterey Peninsula, first lit in 1855, run by the City of Pacific Grove as a small museum.
items.notes: Tickets on site only. Closed Thanksgiving and the day after.

items.name: Asilomar State Beach
items.hours: 8 AM–Sunset
items.best_time: Low tide for tidepools; stay well back from surf on high-swell days.
items.description: State beach on Pacific Grove's west shore with dunes, rocky tidepools and a coastal trail next to the Asilomar Conference Grounds.
items.notes: State Parks closes the beach and Coast Trail during high-surf advisories.

items.name: Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park
items.address: Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park, Big Sur, CA
items.hours: 8am to Sunset
items.best_time: Check Caltrans Highway 1 status and the park alert banner the same morning before driving south.
items.description: Redwood-and-river state park 26 miles south of Carmel on Highway 1 (near mile marker 47.2); there is no ocean access inside the park.
items.notes: Six trails remain closed after the Timber Fire (Pfeiffer Falls, Valley View, Oak Grove, Mt. Manuel, Big Sur River Gorge, Pine Ridge), and storms close the park; check State Parks' status before driving down.

items.name: Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park (McWay Falls)
items.address: Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park (McWay Falls), Big Sur, CA
items.hours: 8am to Sunset
items.best_time: Midday light for the McWay Falls overlook; check Highway 1 status first.
items.description: Big Sur state park 37 miles south of Carmel where a short trail leads to a viewpoint of McWay Falls dropping toward a cove.
items.notes: No beach access at McWay Falls. Highway 1 south of Nepenthe closes after heavy rain; check Caltrans first.

items.name: Big Sur coast drive (Highway 1)
items.address: Big Sur coast drive (Highway 1), Big Sur, CA
items.best_time: Check the Caltrans road-conditions page the morning of; start early to allow for one-way traffic control stops.
items.description: Scenic coastal drive south from Carmel on State Route 1 past Rocky Creek, Point Sur and into Big Sur.
items.notes: Caltrans runs one-way traffic control at several points and closes stretches after storms; check its road conditions page before you go.

items.name: Elkhorn Slough Reserve
items.hours: Wed–Sun 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; closed Mon & Tue
items.best_time: Wednesday–Sunday; early in the day for birding. Check in at the Visitor Center before hiking.
items.description: State ecological reserve on the estuary inland from Moss Landing with about five miles of trails through marsh, oak woodland and grassland, all starting from the Visitor Center.
items.notes: Closed Mondays and Tuesdays; no dogs.

items.name: Dennis the Menace Playground
items.hours: 10 a.m. to dusk; daily Memorial Day–Labor Day; closed non-holiday Tuesdays Labor Day–Memorial Day
items.best_time: Weekday mornings after the 10 a.m. opening; avoid Tuesdays from September to late May.
items.description: City playground in El Estero Park, opened in 1956 with creative input from Dennis the Menace cartoonist Hank Ketcham. It sits on Pearl Street beside Sollecito Ballpark and the Monterey Youth Center.
items.notes: Closed on Tuesdays (except holidays) from Labor Day to Memorial Day.

items.name: El Estero Park & Lake El Estero
items.address: Del Monte and Camino Aguajito, Monterey, CA 93940
items.cost: Free (park); boating concession price not published
items.hours: City parks closed 10 p.m.–6 a.m.; El Estero Snack Bar open weekends year round (summer Tue–Sun 11 a.m.–5 p.m.)
items.best_time: Pair with Dennis the Menace Playground; walk the lake loop or fish from the Pearl Street piers.
items.description: A 45-acre city park around Lake El Estero with picnic areas, an exercise course, fishing piers and a boating concession. The lake is stocked several times a year; anglers 16 and older need a California fishing license.
items.notes: A boating concession rents on the lake; the City doesn't publish its hours or prices ((831) 375-1484).

items.name: Monterey Skate Park
items.hours: Daily 9 a.m. until dusk
items.best_time: Daylight hours; it closes at dusk.
items.description: City skate park for skateboarders and in-line skaters, next to Lake El Estero behind Sollecito Ballpark. Local skaters helped design it.
items.notes: Inside El Estero Park.

items.name: MY Museum (Monterey County Youth Museum)
items.hours: Wed–Sun 10am–5pm; closed New Year's Day, Easter, Thanksgiving, Christmas
items.best_time: Rainy days or weekday mornings; a few minutes' walk from Dennis the Menace Playground.
items.description: Nonprofit hands-on children's museum in downtown Monterey with play exhibits, art-making and circle-time programs included in admission.
items.notes: Open Christmas Eve 10am–3pm and New Year's Eve 12:30–3pm; closed Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's Day.

items.name: Monterey Public Library
items.hours: Mon 2pm–6pm; Tue–Sat 10am–6pm; Sun closed
items.best_time: Tuesday–Saturday; closed Sundays. 2026 closures include Nov 26–27 and Dec 24–26.
items.description: City library in Old Monterey with a children's area and local history resources. A bookmobile also runs on a separate schedule.
items.notes: Closed 26–27 November and 24–26 December.

items.name: Historic gardens of Old Monterey (Monterey State Historic Park)
items.address: Historic gardens of Old Monterey (Monterey State Historic Park), Monterey, CA
items.hours: Gardens open daily, availability subject to events and weather
items.best_time: Daytime walk between downtown adobes; pair with the Path of History markers.
items.description: California State Parks maintains walled gardens behind several historic adobes in downtown Monterey, some with fountains and arbors. No reservations are needed.
items.notes: Several gardens across the historic park; open subject to events and weather.

items.name: Pacific Biological Laboratories (Ed Ricketts' Lab) tours
items.cost: Free public tours; private tours $100 for 1–4 people + $15/person
items.hours: Free tours second Saturday, January–November, 10:00 a.m. and 11:30 a.m.; open hours 12:00–4:00 p.m.
items.best_time: Second Saturday of the month (not December); reserve ahead.
items.description: Docent-led tours of the former lab of marine biologist Ed Ricketts, linked to John Steinbeck and the founding of the Monterey Jazz Festival. The city says tours may suit ages 10 and up.
items.notes: Free tours on the second Saturday, January–November; reserve ahead.

items.name: Old Monterey Jail
items.hours: 7 days a week, 10 am–4 pm
items.best_time: Combine with Colton Hall next door during the same 10–4 window.
items.description: Granite city jail built in 1854 and used until 1956, now open to the public with stories of Gold Rush-era inmates.

items.name: Monterey Museum of Art – Pacific Street
items.cost: Adults $15; 18 and under, students w/ID, active military w/ID, members: Free
items.hours: Thu–Sun 11:00 am–5:00 pm
items.best_time: Thursday–Sunday. Closed Nov 26, 2026 and Dec 21, 2026–Jan 6, 2027.
items.description: Art museum across from Colton Hall showing American and California painting, photography and contemporary art. It runs drop-in Free Family Fun Days nearly every month.
items.notes: Closed Thanksgiving and from 21 December 2026 to 6 January 2027. Free for up to four with SNAP/EBT (Museums for All).

items.name: Monterey Sports Center
items.cost: Drop-in: 2 & under free; youth (3–12) $12; teen $13; adult (18–61) $17; senior $12 (residents $1 less)
items.hours: Mon–Fri 5:30 a.m.–9:00 p.m.; Sat–Sun 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; pool closes 30 min earlier
items.best_time: Weekends 8–5 for families; closed Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day.
items.description: City-run recreation center whose drop-in pass covers two indoor pools, gym, fitness areas, group classes, saunas and a sun deck. Photo ID is required at entry.
items.notes: Closed Thanksgiving and Christmas. Pool schedules vary.

items.name: Old Monterey Marketplace & Farmers Market
items.address: Alvarado Street between Del Monte and Pearl, Monterey
items.hours: Tuesdays, year round, rain or shine: Oct–Apr 4:00–7:00pm; May–Sep 4:00–8:00pm
items.best_time: Tuesday late afternoon; arrive near 4pm for produce.
items.description: Certified farmers market established in 1991 that fills about 3½ blocks of Alvarado Street every Tuesday with produce, baked goods, food vendors and crafts.

site_link.label: Every Monterey County farmers market, day by day

items.name: Alvarado Street & downtown Old Monterey
items.best_time: Evenings for dining; Tuesdays for the market.
items.description: Downtown Monterey's historic main street, named for Alta California governor Juan Bautista Alvarado and surrounded by restaurants, cafés and shops near Colton Hall and the state park adobes. The business association's dining guide includes a late-night category.
items.notes: Official = Old Monterey Business Association site. Dining guide: https://www.oldmonterey.org/dining

items.name: Lighthouse Avenue (Lighthouse District, New Monterey)
items.address: Lighthouse Avenue, New Monterey, Monterey, CA 93940
items.best_time: Lunch or dinner before or after Cannery Row; three blocks uphill from it.
items.description: An eight-block stretch of Lighthouse Avenue in New Monterey with more than two dozen pubs, restaurants and cafés plus independent shops. It is three blocks from Cannery Row.
items.notes: Site run by the New Monterey Business Association. Dining guide: https://lighthousedistrict.net/dining

items.name: Golden State Theatre
items.best_time: Show nights; if not sold out, tickets go on sale at the venue an hour before doors.
items.description: Historic downtown theatre on Alvarado Street hosting touring concerts, comedy and film screenings.
items.notes: Ticket prices vary by show; the box office is on (831) 649-1070.

items.name: MPC Theatre Company – Morgan Stock Stage
items.hours: Performances Thu–Sat 7 PM, Sun 2 PM (during runs)
items.best_time: During spring and fall runs (e.g. March 11–21 and April 15–25, 2027).
items.description: Monterey Peninsula College's theatre company stages plays and musicals on the 300-seat Morgan Stock Stage on campus.
items.notes: Plays run in the spring and fall seasons; spring 2027 tickets go on sale in February.

skipped.reason: In Santa Cruz — out of scope per brief

skipped.name: Bixby Creek Bridge
skipped.reason: No official visitor page found; covered by Big Sur Highway 1 drive item

skipped.name: Moss Landing (harbor/State Beach)
skipped.reason: Not researched to official-page standard in time; Elkhorn Slough covers the area

skipped.name: Monterey Live (music venue)
skipped.reason: No official site found; only a stale third-party listing (414 Alvarado St) with no upcoming events. Treat as likely closed/unverifiable.

skipped.name: Downtown Monterey wine trail
skipped.reason: No official wine trail for the City of Monterey found; Monterey County Vintners only has a county-wide tasting-room directory. Individual tasting rooms would be business picks.

skipped.name: MMA La Mirada
skipped.reason: Official site says it opens only for special museum events/programs and appointments — not a drop-in attraction. Noted under Monterey Museum of Art.

skipped.name: Monterey Peninsula College planetarium
skipped.reason: No official MPC page found for public planetarium shows.

skipped.name: Osio Theater
skipped.reason: official price and about pages return 404

skipped.reason: event venue; nothing to do there without an event
